definitions.definition: "Artificial intelligence" means a machine-based system that makes predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments.

"Generative artificial intelligence" means an artificial system that: (i) is trained on data; (ii) interacts with a person using text, audio, or visual communication; and (iii) generates non-scripted outputs similar to outputs created by a human, with limited or no human oversight.

note: Quoted from S.B. 149 (2024 General Session) as amended by the Senate committee amendments of 2-8-2024 (document-2.pdf); the introduced text (document-1.pdf) has the same wording for both definitions. The enrolled bill is not among the stored files. The definitions are in the bill's own numbering: new Section 13-70-101 in a Chapter 70, Artificial Intelligence Policy Act, and new Section 13-2-12; the record's identifier gives the codified chapter as Title 13, Chapter 72. Section 13-70-101(3) also defines 'artificial intelligence technology' (a computer system, application or other product that uses or incorporates one or more forms of artificial intelligence), which has no term group; Section 76-2-107(1) refers back to the definition of 'generative artificial intelligence' in Section 13-2-12. The bill does not define 'AI system', 'model' or the other groups.
